description: Every error counter the host channel adapters expose, transport layer and physical layer, each paired with the exact list of rails behind it. Absorbs the former 'Link Signal Quality' board. Link-down events live on the Link Flaps board; backpressure lives on the Congestion board.

options.content:
Host-HCA InfiniBand boards  |  Rail State & Cabling  ·  Blast Radius  ·  Link Flaps  ·  Port Errors  ·  Congestion & Throughput  ·  Signal Quality  ·  Worst Offenders
Source: ib_hca_* counters read on every DGX tray by node-exporter, four rails per tray. Every number on the left of a band is backed by the table beside it, built from the identical selector — the table footer prints the row count.

panels.title: Transport-layer errors reported by the host adapter

panels.description: Packets the adapter received and could not accept. The strongest single signal of a bad cable or transceiver. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with receive errors

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero counter.

panels.title: Rails with receive errors — the exact rails

panels.description: The adapter saw a packet out of sequence and asked for a retransmit. Indicates loss on the path. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with packet-sequence errors

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero counter.

panels.title: Rails with packet-sequence errors — the exact rails

panels.description: NAKs sent because a packet arrived out of order. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with out-of-sequence NAKs

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero counter.

panels.title: Rails with out-of-sequence NAKs — the exact rails

panels.description: The peer retransmitted a request the adapter had already handled, usually because the original acknowledgement was lost. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with duplicate requests

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero counter.

panels.title: Rails with duplicate requests — the exact rails

panels.description: The adapter gave up waiting for an acknowledgement. Often downstream congestion rather than a local fault. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with local ACK timeouts

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero counter.

panels.title: Rails with local ACK timeouts — the exact rails

panels.description: A work request completed in error on the requester or the responder side. These surface to the application as RDMA failures. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with completion-queue errors

panels.description: One row per rail with a requester or responder CQE error. Built from the identical selector as the number on the left, so the row count equals it.
panels.title: Rails with completion-queue errors — the exact rails (requester + responder)

panels.description: 8b/10b or 64b/66b decode failures on the wire — the lowest-level cable-quality signal. Source: ib_hca_symbol_error, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The union of this counter with link-error recovery and receive errors is on the Signal Quality board. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with symbol errors

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has a non-zero symbol-error counter — the fleet is clean at the physical layer.

panels.title: Rails with symbol errors — the exact rails

panels.description: Rate of change of each error counter across the fleet. Flat lines mean the damage is historic; a rising line means it is happening now.
